# Section 1: Spring Boot 4 Quick Start

# 5\. Spring Boot Overview

## Spring in a Nutshell

* Very popular framework for building java applications  
* Provides a large number of helper classes and annotations.

## Problem

* Building a traditional spring application is really hard  
  * Which JAR dependencies do i need  
  * How do I set up configuration (xml or java)?  
  * How do I install the server? (Tomcat, JBoss, etc..)

## Spring Boot Solution

* Make it easier to get started with Spring development  
* Minimize the amount of manual configuration  
  * Perform auto-configuration based on props files and JAR classpath  
* Help to resolve dependency conflicts (Maven or Gradle)  
* Provide an embedded HTTP server so you can get started quickly  
  * Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow, …

## 

## Spring Boot and Spring

* Spring Boot uses Spring behind the scenes  
* Spring Boot simply makes it easier to use Spring

## Spring Initializer

* [http\://start.spring.io](http://start.spring.io)

## Spring Boot Embedded Server

* Provide an embedded HTTP Server so you can get started quickly  
  * Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow, …  
* No need to install a server seperately  
* Self-contained unit \- Nothing else to install

![][image1]

## Running Spring Boot Apps

1) Spring Boot apps can be run standalone (includes embedded server)  
* Run the Spring Boot app from IDE or command-lin  
  * java \-jar mycoolapp.jar

2) Spring Boot apps can also be deployed in the traditional way  
* Deploy WAR file to an external server: Tomcat, JBoss, WebSphere, etc..  
* WAR: Web Application Archive

![][image2]

## Spring Boot FAQ \#1

* Q: Does Spring Boot replace Spring MVC, Spring REST etc ..?  
  * No. Instead, Spring Boot actually uses those technologies  
* Q: Does Spring Boot run code faster than regular Spring code?  
  * No. Behind the scene, Spring Boot uses same code of Spring Framework  
* Q: Do I need a special IDE for Spring Boot?  
  * No. You can use any IDE for Spring Boot apps  
  * The Spring team provides a free Spring Tool suite(STS) \[IDE plugins\]

## 

## Quick Work on Maven

* When building your java project, you may need additional JAR files  
  * Eg: Spring, Hibernate, Commons Logging, JSON etc.  
* One approach is to download the JAR files from each project web site  
* Manually add the JAR files to your build path/classpath

## Maven Solution

* Tell maven the projects you are working with (dependencies)  
  * Spring, Hibernate, etc..  
* Maven will go out and download the JAR files for those projects for you  
* And Maven will make those JAR files available during compile/run  
* Think of maven as your friendly helper / personal shopper

## Spring Boot initializer Demo

* Project: Maven  
* Language: Java  
* Spring Boot: Choose the latest released version. Avoid the ‘Snapshot” versions since they are alpha/beta  
* Artifact: name of the application/project

## Spring Projects

* Spring Projects are additional Spring modules built-on top of the core Spring Framework  
* Only use what you need:  
  * Spring Cloud, Spring Data  
  * Spring Batch, Spring Security  
  * Spring Web Services, Spring LDAP  
  * Others…

## What is Maven?

* Maven is a Project Management tool  
* Most popular use of Maven is for build management and dependencies  
* What problems does Maven solves:  
  * When building your java project, you may need additional JAR files  
  * Eg: Spring, Hibernate, Commons Logging, JSON etc..  
* One approach is to download the JAR files from each project web site  
* Manually add the JAR files to your build path / classpath

How Maven works  
![][image3]

Building and Running

* When you build and run you app  
  * Maven will handle class/ build path for you  
  * Based on config file, Maven will add JAR files accordingly

## Maven Project Structure

Standard Directory Structure Benefits

* Most major IDEs have built-in support for Maven  
  * Eclipse, IntelliJ, NetBeans, etc  
  * IDEs can easily read/import Maven Project  
* Maven Projects are portable  
  * Developers can easily share projects between IDEs  
  * No need to fight about which IDE is the best.  
    

Advantage of Maven

* Dependency Management  
  * Maven will find JAR files for you  
  * No more missing JARs  
* Building and Running your Project  
  * No more build path/ classpath issues  
* Standard directory structure

Personal Best Maven Benefits

* Once you learn Maven, you can join a new project and be productive  
* You can build and run a project with minimal local configuration

## Maven Key Concepts

* POM File \- pom.xml  
* Project Coordinates

POM File

* Project Object Model file  
* Configuration file your project  
  * Basically your ‘shopping list’ for Maven


![][image4]

Project Coordinates

* Uniquely identifies a project  
* Similar to GPS coordinates for your house: latitude / longitude  
* Precise information for finding your house (city, street, house \#)

![][image5]	

Project coordinates \- elements

* GroupId: Name of company, group or organization. Use reverse domain name  
* Artifact ID: Name of the project: mycoolapp  
* Version:   
  * A specific release version like: 1.0, 1.6, 2.0.  
  *  If the project is under active development then: 1.0-SNAPSHOT.   
  * Version is optional. Best practice is to include the version (repeatable builds)

May see this referred to as: GAV

* Group ID, Artifact ID, Version  
* What's your GAV ? What’s the GAV for the project?

How to find Dependency Coordinates

* Option 1: Visit the project page ([spring.io](http://spring.io), [hibernate.or](http://hibernate.or), etc)  
* Option 2: visit [https\://central.sonatype.com](https://central.sonatype.com) (easy approach)

Exploring Spring Boot Project Files

mvnw: Maven Wrapper files

* Mvnw allows you to run a Maven project  
* No need to have Maven installed or present on your path  
* If correct version is not found on your computer  
  * Automatically downloads correct version and runs Maven  
* 2 files are provided  
  * mvnw.cmd for MS Windows : mvnw clean compile test  
  * [mvnw.sh](http://mvnw.sh) for Linux/Mac: ./mvnw clean compile test  
* If you already have Maven installed previously   
  * Then you can ignore/delete the mvnw files  
* Just use Maven as you normally would  
  * mvn clean compile test

Maven POM file  
	Pom.xml includes info that you entered at Spring Initializer website

\<groupId\>org.springframework.boot\</groupId\>  
\<artifactId\>spring-boot-maven-plugin\</artifactId\>

To package executable jar or war archive. Can also easily run the app.  
	./mvnw package  
	./mvnw spring-boot:run

If maven is already installed, then don’t need mvnw  
	mvn package  
	mvn spring-boot:run

	

## Exploring Spring Boot Project Files

Static: By default, Spring Boot will load static resources from “/static” directory  
Egs of status resources: HTML files, CSS, Javascript, images, etc..

src/main/webapp: Only works with WAR packaging. Silently ignored by most build tolls if you generate JAR

Templates

* By default, Spring Boot will load templates from “./templates” directory  
* Spring Boot includes auto-configuration for the following template engines  
* FreeMarker  
* Thymeleaf  
* Mustache

## Spring Boot Starters

	

| Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| spring-boot-starter-webmvc | Building web apps, includes REST, tomcat default embedded server |
| spring-boot-starter-security | Adding spring security support |
| spring-boot-starter-data-jpa | Spring database support with jpa and hibernate |

View Starter dependencies  
	View \> tool Windows \> maven \> dependencies

Spring Boot Starter Parent

* Spring Boot provides a “Starter Parent”  
* This is a special starter that provides Maven defaults  
* Maven defaults defined in the starter parent  
  * Default compiler level  
  * UTF-8 source encoding  
  * Others…  
* Default configuration of Spring Boot plugin  
  * Group-id: org.springframework.boot  
  * Artifact-id: spring-boot-maven-plugin  
  * Mvn spring-boot:run

Benefit of Spring Boot Starter Parent

* Default  Maven configuration: java version, UTF-encoding etc  
* Dependency Management  
  * Use version on parent only  
  * spring-boot-starter-\* dependencies inherits version from parent  
* Default configuration of Spring Boot plugin

## Spring Boot Dev Tools

* Problem: when running spring boot applications  
  * If you make changes to your source code  
    * Then you’ve to manually restart your application.   
* Solution:   
  * Spring-boot-devtools  
  * Automatically restarts your application when code is updated.   
  * Simply add the dependency to your POM file  
  * No need to write additional code 🙂  
  * For IntelliJ, need to set additional configurations  
    * Settings | Build, Execution, Deployment | Compiler | Build project automatically

Spring Boot Actuator

* Exposes endpoints to monitor and manage your application  
* You easily get DevOps functionality out of the box  
* Simply add the dependency to you POM file  
* REST endpoints are automatically added to your application 

| Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| /health | Health information about your application |

## Spring Boot Actuator Security

* YOu many not want to access all this information  
* Add dependency: spring-boot-starter-security  
  * Default username: user  
  * Password: check console logs for password

## Running from command-line

* Spring Boot apps are self contained  
  * JAR includes application code AND the server  
* Option 1: java \-jar mycoolapp.jar	note: make sure jar exist, if not ./mvnw clean package  
* Option 2: maven plugin: ./mvnw spring-boot:run

If maven is already installed, then can delete mvnw AND mvnw.cmd,   
And just run mvn spring-boot:run

## Spring Boot Properties

* About 1000+ properties  
* Teh properties are roughly group into the following categories  
  * Core: logging levels  
  * Web: se  
  * Security  
  * Data  
  * Actuator  
  * Integration  
  * Devtools  
  * testing
